name: MESSENGER
first: First spacecraft to orbit Mercury; first complete surface map of the innermost planet
description: MESSENGER (MErcury Surface, Space ENvironment, GEochemistry, and Ranging) used six gravity assists across seven years — Earth, Venus twice, Mercury three times — to slow into Mercury orbit on 2011-03-18. Sunshade-protected with one side at 370 °C and the other at -45 °C. Discoveries included water ice in permanently shadowed polar craters, previously unknown “hollows” geological features, and confirmation that Mercury's iron core occupies ~85 % of the planet's radius (the largest core-to-radius ratio of any planet in the solar system). Mission ended with a controlled impact onto Mercury’s surface 2015-04-30 after fuel ran out.

events.label: LAUNCH
events.note: Delta II 7925H lifts MESSENGER on a six-flyby trajectory.

events.label: EARTH GRAVITY ASSIST
events.note: First of six assists to slow the trajectory enough to enter Mercury orbit.

events.label: MERCURY ORBIT INSERTION
events.note: Main-engine burn places MESSENGER into Mercury orbit after seven years of cruise.
